NOTES 
(1) Enforcement Possibilities. For now, set aside the court's rulings on 
restitution for the purchasers and the rental-value charge, and consider only 
the ruling that the purchasers 
were entitled to rescission. (As to monetary 
adjustments, see below.) 
Suppose that the buyers had learned of the water problem earlier, and 
had refused to take a conveyance. 
Suppose also that the court had ruled 
otherwise on the issue of mistake. It would follow that the sellers could have 
recovered damages based on the contract price. Does it also follow that th 
sellers could have won an order for specific performance, as is usual for 
contracts for real-property transfers? Recall the element of judicial discretion 
in actions for specific performance, 
and see McKinnon v. Benedict, p. 641 
above. 
(2) The Converse Case. Changing the facts in Renner, suppose that the 
buyers' test drilling had disclosed not only an ample and accessible supply of 
water but also valuable minerals. 
Then the sellers, not the buyers, would 
seek to rescind the contract. What are the chances that action would succeed? 
"[I]t is commonly understood that the seller of farm land generally cannot 
avoid the contract of sale upon later discovery by both parties that the land 
contains valuable mineral deposits, even though the price was negotiated on 
the basic assumption that the land was suitable only for farming and th 
effect on the agreed exchange of performances is material." Restatement 
§ 154 cmt. a. Can this be explained on any ground other than caveat vendor? 
SECTION 2. 
UNILATERAL MISTAKE 
Reprieve under the doctrine 
of unilateral 
mistake is most commonly 
sought in situations involving 
erroneous bids, 
as in Elsinore School 
District v. Kastorff, p. 209, where a bidder for building work got relief for 
his mistaken offer. Yet construction 
bids are 
not the only site of 
application for the doctrine 
of unilateral 
mistake, 
as our next ca e 
illustrates. When reading the opinion below, take note of how the court 
applies the doctrine variably to the questions of formation and avoidance.
